title: Do Mandatory Disclosure Requirements for Private Firms Increase the Propensity of Going Public?

issues.description: None of the twelve named .dta tables is included in the release. The driver has required U.S. BioMedTracker/Compustat and separate Orbis/Amadeus Europe/Germany/FX panels; exact fields, producers, full coverage and current access remain unverified. The additional direct merge/append inputs identified by source review are included in the requirements.

The 19 branch setup lines contain literal cd placeholders. Stage the driver and exact-named inputs together and use a relative working-directory setting in a working copy before attempting the workflow.

The same Germany propensity-score sample is saved as PS Sample Germany.dta and consumed twice as PS sample Germany.dta. Matching the two consumer spellings to the producer capitalization is a routine case-sensitive path repair if the same staged file is intended.

The disclosure input is consumed under num_disclosure, num_disclosures, disclosure, phase2_disc and phaseabove_disc spellings. The absent input namespace prevents confirming whether these are separate fields or any intended alias mapping.

IPO Dates JAR Final.dta is described as Compustat IPO dates manually matched to BioMedTracker names. The match procedure and covered firm universe are not supplied; the local COMP.FUNDA candidate lacks a verified IPO-date field or matching crosswalk.

The project-level portfolio, indication competition, appended IPO supplement and acquisition-year tables are separate inputs. Their exact schemas, producers, and ownership of fields such as orphan_drug are not fully specified by the source files.

All Europe.dta, Germany Sample Competitiveness.dta and All Europe v2.dta are distinct prepared inputs with different source populations, periods and fields. Their exact BvD query/merge preparation, country coverage and full panel histories are unverified.

The FX file is described as annual USD/EUR rates, but the code merges by year and multiplies every monetary variable by usd_eur, while applying EXCHRATE first to non-EUR observations. The series identities, field ownership, directions and units are unresolved; no replacement formula is inferred.

Several calls use xi: reg ... , r absorb(company) cluster(company). Stata 18 documentation associates absorb() with areg, while the supplied command is reg. This is an unresolved compatibility question; no command substitution or estimator test was made.
psmatch2 is required to produce the German propensity-score sample but is unavailable in the current Stata command lookup. Its documented SSC route makes this a software setup task.

The installed ivreg2 4.1.12 help and ado require ranktest and check a minimum version. The exact `which ranktest` check succeeds, but it does not report the installed ranktest version; compatibility with the package's Stata 18 call path therefore remains unverified.

our main hypothesis, discussed in Section 6.3. In particular, we utilize the variation in
size thresholds for required disclosure across firms in twelve EU member states: Austria,
Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, Sweden,
and the United Kingdom. In order to do so, we use data from the Bureau van Dijk Orbis
database from 2002 to 2019, and run the following regression:

                  IPOi,t = α + βThreshold j,i,t−1 + γ 0 Xi,t + µi + πj × ηt + εi,t .                (4)

The above specification is similar to that of Breuer et al. (2019), which also utilizes variation
in disclosure thresholds, however we consider the firm-year level and examine a different
outcome.43 In equation (4), Threshold j,i,t−1 is an indicator variable that takes a value of
1 if firm i in country j crossed country j’s disclosure threshold in year t − 1 or if the firm
stayed past the disclosure threshold for two or more consecutive years, and 0 otherwise. (The
results are also consistent if we define this variable contemporaneously.) The idea is that a
private firm that becomes subject to the disclosure requirements for its respective country

steps: Ask the authors for the exact named prepared tables or an already authorized compatible release, plus a data dictionary, producer/processing notes, join-key definitions and full year/firm coverage for each file.

Confirm disclosure spellings without assuming num_disclosure, num_disclosures or disclosure are aliases; identify which table owns orphan_drug; preserve the separate project, firm-year and denominator table units.

For IPO Dates JAR Final.dta, request the manual Compustat-to-BioMedTracker matching rule and firm universe. The catalogued COMP.FUNDA file is only a candidate and does not establish the IPO-date field or crosswalk.

For Appended Data IPOs BMT.dta and acquisition_year.dta, request their producer notes and exact field definitions, including the distinction among risk_drug_acq, risk_drug_acq_y, late_drugacq and late_drugacq_y.

Treat the datasheet's historical BioMedTracker and Compustat subscription routes as provenance. It does not establish a current access barrier; if only raw sources are available, first request author-provided extraction and matching instructions rather than independently rebuilding the inputs.
validation: Before analysis, use bounded metadata checks on each obtained .dta file to confirm exact filename, readability, required variables, key types, duplicates and year coverage, including the panel history needed by source-coded lags.

Check that author-prepared files preserve the documented firm-year versus project-year units and the manually matched IPO-date relationship; retain all authored tables and definitions without changing samples or estimators.

validation: Use bounded metadata checks to confirm each table's expected fields, identifiers and supported year/country coverage; verify the Germany table contains the merged IPO and Amadeus fields used by both industry-definition blocks.

For the 2002-2019 table, verify the author's original currency field and treatment history needed by the code's two-consecutive-year L/L2 construction; do not extrapolate beyond the supported source period.
